newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles panel approves sports arena proposal.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles panel approves sports arena proposal.

text.p: A panel of city officials on Monday approved a plan to build a sports and entertainment complex in downtown Los Angeles, forwarding the controversial proposal to the City Council for review.
The Los Angeles City Council's ad hoc committee on the arena proposal approved the business plan, and urged the Council to accept the proposal and finalise the agreement.
The City Council was expected to act on the proposal on Wednesday, officials said.
The committee's decision capped months of negotiations over the development of the proposed downtown arena for the Los Angeles Kings hockey team and the Lakers basketball team.
City negotiators said on Monday that the basic framework of the deal was now in place, adding that the transaction would bolster the local economy by creating jobs.

Under the proposal, the city would contribute $70.5 million to the project. The city's contribution would be funded with a taxable debt financing of $50.5 million and $20 million from a bond reserve fund, city negotiators said in a report.

The average annual cost of the city's contribution was estimated to be $6.8 million. This amount was expected to be fully recovered from tax revenues generated by the arena and from other sources, city negotiators said.
Critics of the plan said it put city taxpayers at risk.
